newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Eurodollar, Euroyen softer in thin pre-X'mas.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Eurodollar, Euroyen softer in thin pre-X'mas.

text.p: SIMEX Eurodollar futures were a touch softer in extremely thin pre-Christmas conditions, with Euroyen unchanged, thinned by a holiday in Japan, traders said.
Eurodollars adopted a slightly negative slant in early trade tracking developments in Chicago after U.S. treasuries reacted to the Federal Reserve's tighter fiscal policy bias.
In Federal Open Market Committee (FMOC) minutes of a November 13 meeting, it was shown on Friday that officials voted unanimously to hold short-term U.S. interest rates steady.
March Eurodollars ended at 94.45, unchanged against its previous IMM close, and June finished at 94.31, down from 94.32.
"The market went a little weaker following the news, but it's difficult to see the impact with such thin liquidity," a trader with a Japanese bank said.
He predicted more listless trade for this week with Monday's U.S. economic figures, such as personal income and spending data, unlikely to set meaningful direction.
Euroyen activity was similarly muted, dampened by a public holiday in Japan and the closure of the Tokyo stock market.
Prices were mostly stagnant over the session although the outlook was helped by a recovery in the Nikkei 225 average last Friday, when it closed 119.79 points higher at 19,690.46.
But vulnerability to the downside, after the index breached critical 20,000 point support, kept Euroyen defensive.
June Euroyen futures ended at 99.41 against its previous IMM settlement at 99.42. September closed unchanged at 99.31.
The Japanese government bond futures market was closed in line with Tokyo.
SIMEX futures will trade regular hours on Christmas Eve, with shortened hours for Euroyen and JGB's on Christmas Day.
